title: Concurrent same-host web crawler
prompt: Given a start URL and an HtmlParser/LinkProvider (getUrls(url) -> list[str]), return every URL reachable from the start URL whose hostname equals the start URL's hostname, each exactly once. Start single-threaded (BFS), then make it concurrent.
levels: L1 (sync): BFS/DFS from startUrl; filter by urlparse(start).hostname; strip #fragments before dedupe (fastprep variant); return list/set. Code must actually run (CodeSignal/CoderPad).
L2 (threads): ThreadPoolExecutor workers + thread-safe frontier queue + visited set with atomic check-and-add; correct termination when queue empty AND no task in flight.
L3 (async variant): rewrite with asyncio (Anthropic 2025-02 thread: 'sync first, then async'; LC 2026-01: 'thread pool executors and asyncio').
Depth-limited variant (Databricks): crawl only to depth k/h, then multithread it.
followups: thread pool size for IO-bound work; why threads help despite GIL
politeness: per-host rate limit / max concurrency
bottlenecks (network, disk) and scaling to many machines (Databricks HLD-with-code round)
notes: Most-reported practical question across labs. Anthropic: FH x4 (LC 2025-05, 2026-01, 2026-02 mention; 1p3a 2025-02) + AGG (inbyte 'high freq' Sep 2025-May 2026; prachub 2026-08 'Make a Hostname-Limited Crawler Concurrent'; hellointerview staff report 2026-03). OpenAI: 1p3a high-frequency summary (2025 Q3) says runnable crawler in Python, part 2 multithreading for IO blocking. Databricks FH x3 (depth-limited + multithreaded). Glean AGG: rate-limited Wikipedia crawler (2026-02). Mirrors LeetCode 1242.

title: Dependency-aware task / job scheduler (topological order, failures, concurrency)
prompt: Tasks declare dependencies; run or order them so every task runs after its prerequisites, handle failures (skip dependents), detect cycles, and optionally run independent tasks concurrently.
levels: L1: deterministic topological order (ties broken lexicographically - OpenAI 2026-08 'lexicographically smallest topological order').
L2: failures - a failed task marks all transitive dependents failed/skipped (Perplexity 'Task Dependencies and Failure').
L3: concurrent execution of ready tasks with a worker pool (OpenAI 'Dependency-Aware Concurrent Tool Scheduler', Codex multi-agent request scheduler).
Variants: deadlines ('Schedule Ready Tasks by Deadline', Scale AI); cycle detect-and-break in pod dependencies (Together AI); to-do list with dependencies (Perplexity).
followups: cycle detection and reporting the cycle
incremental add of tasks while running
notes: All AGG (prachub/darkinterview), no FH post found; dates 2025-08 to 2026-08. Some entries may be design-flavoured; the Scale/Perplexity/OpenAI ones are labelled coding/technical screen.

title: CodeSignal in-memory record database (fields, scan, TTL, backup/restore or compare-and-set/history)
prompt: CodeSignal Industry Coding Framework task, 90 min, 4 levels that unlock on passing tests. Records keyed by string, each holding field->value pairs. Two reported shapes: (A) classic set/get/delete -> scan -> TTL -> backup/restore; (B) newer command-array form with COMPARE_AND_SET/COMPARE_AND_DELETE and historical reads.
levels: Variant A L1: set(key, field, value) -> ''; get(key, field) -> value or ''; delete(key, field) -> 'true'/'false'.
Variant A L2: scan(key) -> 'f1(v1), f2(v2)' fields sorted lexicographically; scan_by_prefix(key, prefix) same format; missing record -> ''.

Variant A L3: timestamped twins set_at(key, field, value, ts), set_at_with_ttl(key, field, value, ts, ttl) alive on [ts, ts+ttl), delete_at, get_at, scan_at, scan_by_prefix_at; timestamps strictly increase; old methods must keep working (backward compatibility).

Variant A L4: backup(ts) -> number of non-empty, non-expired records (as string), saving each field's REMAINING lifespan; restore(ts, ts_to_restore) loads the latest backup taken before ts_to_restore and re-bases expiries: new_expiry = restore_ts + remaining.

Variant B (inbyte, Anthropic 2025-10..2026-05): commands arrive as arrays with ms timestamps; L1 SET/GET/DELETE plus COMPARE_AND_SET(expected, new) and COMPARE_AND_DELETE(expected); L2 SCAN / SCAN_BY_PREFIX sorted; L3 per-field TTL versions; L4 backup/restore with paused TTLs or value-at-past-timestamp queries (gist: 'historical queries'). Exact L4 signature not verified.
Variant C (practice repo only, unverified): set_or_inc / top_n_keys by modification count / lock(caller_id, key) / unlock(key).
followups: speed: all 4 levels in 90 min, score 200-600, ~480-520+ to pass
refactor for later levels (store expiry per field, keep history)
deep copy on backup (shallow copy corrupts snapshots)
notes: Spec text for Variant A matches the widely shared ICF task (REPO: https://github.com/EricZheng0404/LibreSignal Questions/in_memory_database). FH: Blind 2023-10 (4 rounds, 90 min, 'code VERY FAST'). prachub lists Anthropic ONSITE 'Build a Versioned In-Memory Database' (2026-05) and xAI ONSITE 'in-memory database with TTL and backup' (2026-09) - so it is not only an OA. Also used by non-labs (Ramp, Coinbase...). Meta's 'Read Current and Historical Field Values with Expiration' (MLE tech screen 2026-09) looks like the same task (fields + expiry + history) - title-level match only. Our inmem-db page (tables/indexes/transactions) does NOT match - needs its own page.

title: Rate limiter - composite rules, cost budgets, debug-and-optimize
prompt: Cursor screen: from in-memory request logs [user_id, url, body_size_bytes, ts_seconds], enforce limits per user; then generalise into a pluggable rule interface where a request is admitted only if ALL rules pass.
levels: Cursor T1: 3 req/s per user on v1/completions/standard; denied requests are not counted.

Cursor T2: rule interface supporting 7 req/min on an endpoint, 5 req/s on another, a byte-size budget (<=100 bytes/min on an endpoint), and 7 req/hour across ALL endpoints; if any rule denies, the request is not counted by any rule (all-or-nothing).
xAI: per-key fixed-window COST limiter with ALLOW and RESET commands (weights, not counts).
OpenAI: 'Rate Limiter Debug and Optimize' (fix and speed up given code) and 'Implement a Distributed Rate Limiter' (2026-04 screen).
Databricks-adjacent: KV store exposing measure_put_load()/measure_get_load() = average calls over last 5 minutes; follow-up many calls within one second.
notes: Cursor FH (2026-01): interviewer wanted a working solution over complexity; interface + concrete rule classes. Anthropic entry is 'Design a Distributed Rate Limiter' onsite 2026-04 (likely design). Existing rate-limiter page covers algorithms; the lab twist is multi-rule composition, byte budgets and not counting denied requests.

title: Time-versioned key-value store (get value as of time t) with production follow-ups
prompt: set(key, value, timestamp) and get(key, timestamp) returning the value with the largest timestamp <= t ('' if none). OpenAI version uses real float epoch timestamps that may arrive out of order and then drills into testing, clock problems and thread safety.
levels: P1: TimeMap.set(key, value, ts: float), get(key, ts) -> str; out-of-order inserts (bisect.insort); '' when nothing <= ts.
P2: 'How would you test this? How would you mock time?' - inject a time_provider; deterministic tests, no sleeps.
P3: enforce strictly increasing timestamps per key (reject with error vs bump) - clock skew, duplicates.
P4: multi-threaded access - global lock vs per-key lock vs read-write lock vs copy-on-write; write a concurrency test.
Perplexity variant: 'time-versioned KV store with restore' (restore to a past version). Character.ai: 'timestamped key-value map'.
followups: memory growth: compaction of old versions
notes: OpenAI: 1p3a problem page is literally titled 'Resumable Iterator, Unit Tests, Time-Based KV Store, and Concurrency' - so the screen can bundle two tasks. darkinterview labels OpenAI version 'Phone, Onsite ... Reported Aug 2026'; inbyte says most recent Oct 2025. Existing mt-ttl-cache/lru pages do not cover versions-by-time.

title: Durable key-value store: serialize/restore, WAL, crash consistency
prompt: Build a KV store that survives restarts: serialize the whole store to bytes through a provided mock file system and rebuild it (OpenAI), or make a multithreaded single-server store crash-consistent (Baseten), or withstand failures with tight memory (Anyscale).
levels: OpenAI L1: KVStore(file_system) with set/get; shutdown() serializes everything to bytes and saves; restore() rebuilds. No JSON/pickle.
OpenAI L2: keys/values may contain ANY character (delimiters, newlines) -> length-prefixed encoding '<keyLen>:<key><valueLen>:<value>' with 4-byte integer lengths via provided serialize_int helpers.
OpenAI follow-ups: file-size/chunk limits across multiple files, partial writes, corruption detection.
Baseten: multithreaded single-server store that is crash-consistent (WAL + fsync ordering + recovery).
Anyscale (2023): Get/Put that withstands failures with very limited memory.
notes: OpenAI onsite 'Serialize and Restore an In-Memory Key-Value Store' (prachub 2026-09); inbyte: onsite, SWE+infra, most recent Nov 2025. Anthropic's LRU-durability and Databricks' WAL writer are the same skill (see those items).

title: GPU credit ledger (grants with start/expiry, subtract earliest-expiring first, balance at time t)
prompt: Grants of credit are active on [start, expire). Events can arrive out of order. subtract consumes from the active grant that expires earliest (spilling to the next); get_balance(t) reports the balance at time t.
levels: L1: create_grant/add(id, amount, start_ts, expire_ts); get_balance(ts) with no spending.
L2: subtract(amount, ts) consuming earliest-expiring active grants first; same-timestamp order: expiries, then new grants, then subtractions in input order.
L3: events out of order - replay by timestamp (sort add/expire/cost entries, adjust future expiry amounts when spending) - FH 2025-11 warns 'add all then subtract' is wrong.

Variants: subtract returns False when insufficient (FIFO credits) vs balance allowed to go negative and stay negative until later grants cover it (inbyte 'GPU Credit 2'); new-grad version: unsorted post/delete statements, balance at any timestamp (priority queue + tree map).
followups: O(log n) balance queries (prefix sums / segment tree)
notes: FH x3 on LeetCode (2024-11 new grad screen; 2025-10 'expiration_timestamp drove me nuts'; 2025-11 phone). inbyte: 'high freq', phone screen, ~75 min, Apr-Jun 2026. Perplexity has a clone ('CreditTracker with expirations', 2026-04). Not covered by digital-wallet/banking pages.

L2: UNK handling - collapse consecutive UNK (-1) runs into one.
L3: trie for speed; detokenize and round-trip tests ('Debug Tokenization and Detokenization', 2026-07).
Glean: implement BPE (learn merges, encode).

title: IPv4 / CIDR: firewall rule matching (Databricks) and IP range iterator (OpenAI)
prompt: Databricks: rules [(ALLOW|DENY, ip-or-CIDR)] checked in order, first match wins, default deny; access_ok(ip). OpenAI: iterator over IPv4 addresses in 5 unlocking parts.
levels: Databricks L1: parse dotted quad to 32-bit int; CIDR a.b.c.d/p -> [network, broadcast] via mask; /0 and /32 edge cases.
Databricks L2: first-match-wins over ordered rules; also print the index of the deciding rule (2026-02 variant).

OpenAI P1: forward iteration from an IP to 255.255.255.255; P2: reverse to 0.0.0.0; P3: restrict to a CIDR block (size 2^(32-prefix); seed may not be the network address; stop at broadcast/network); P4: step size; P5: not captured.
followups: many rules: sort ranges / trie / interval merge

title: Resumable iterator (get_state/set_state) - list, file, multi-file, 2D/3D, async
prompt: Define an abstract ResumableIterator with __iter__/__next__, get_state() -> dict and set_state(dict). Resuming from ANY captured state must continue exactly where it stopped. Often test-driven: write the tests first.
levels: L1: abstract interface + tests that capture state at every step and resume from each captured state (TDD; 'at least three unit tests' that must pass).
L2: list iterator.
L3: file iterator - state holds a durable byte offset (not an open handle) so a fresh process can reopen and resume.
L4: multi-file iterator (state = file index + offset) / 2D matrix then 3D nested iterator skipping empty sub-lists ('Multi-Dimensional Support').
Async variant: coroutine-based iteration over multiple sources with independent serializable state (hellointerview).
followups: concurrent iterators must not share state
notes: FH: LC 2024-10 ('templatized iterator supporting suspension, resumption' + TDD). hellointerview: 2 OpenAI reports (2024-12 senior, 2025-10 mid). xAI FH 2025-05: 'creating iterators on a list and nested lists'. 1p3a also has an OpenAI thread on 'Iterators, Generators, and Coroutines'.

title: Duplicate file finder (group identical files in a huge tree)
prompt: find_duplicates(root) -> list[list[str]]: walk the tree and group files with byte-identical content; omit singletons; never load whole files into memory.
levels: L1: walk + group by full-content hash (streamed in chunks).
L2: size bucket -> partial hash (first chunk) -> full hash to cut IO.
L3: robustness - permission errors, symlinks (and symlink cycles), hard links, huge files.
L4: parallelize across cores/machines; optionally replace duplicates with hard links.
notes: inbyte: Anthropic 'high freq', phone + onsite, Sep 2025-Jun 2026. A search snippet says dedupe was the 'old' Q2 with a new Q2 after Sep 2025 (the LRU bug-fix+durability) - both still reported in 2026.

title: Spreadsheet with formulas and dependency updates (OpenSheet / Harvey)

title: Concurrent HTTP/API client with retries (fleet actions, parallel downloads)

P2: timeouts, connection errors, invalid JSON -> meaningful output.
P3: reboot many servers concurrently - ThreadPoolExecutor + requests (async + requests blocks the event loop - noted trap).
P4: how to unit test (mock requests, error cases).
Baseten: replace sequential blocking API calls with a thread pool; parallel chunked file download + integrity check.
followups: async vs threads with blocking libs
rate limits of the remote API

title: Profiler: convert sampled call stacks into start/end trace events
prompt: Input: list of Sample(ts, stack) sorted by ts, stack[0] outermost. Output the ordered start/end events a tracing profiler would show.
levels: L1: first sample -> start events outer->inner; between samples keep the longest common prefix; emit end events for popped frames inner->outer, then start events for pushed frames outer->inner; handle recursion (compare by position, not name) and same-timestamp ordering.
L2 (noise filter): a frame must appear in N consecutive samples before it is emitted; start time back-dated to its first sighting.
Other rotations: enter/exit log -> stack at every step with adjacent identical stacks compressed into duration runs; compare by suffix instead of prefix; only the last m frames visible.
followups: flush open frames at the end
notes: FH: LC 2026-02 ('I was asked the Stack Trace problem'). inbyte 'high freq' phone+onsite Sep 2025-Jun 2026; prachub entries 2026-07/08 incl. senior. Signature Anthropic question (also a public 'viral video' rendition on GitHub).

title: CodeSignal bank system (4 levels)
prompt: Timestamps (ms, strictly increasing) on every call. Variant A is the widely shared ICF bank; Variant B (inbyte) replaces immediate transfers with hold + accept.
levels: A-L1: create_account(ts, id)->bool; deposit(ts, id, amount)->new balance|None; transfer(ts, src, dst, amount)->src balance|None (missing account, same account, insufficient funds -> None).
A-L2: top_spenders(ts, n)->['id(total_outgoing)', ...] by outgoing desc, then id asc; outgoing = transfers out + payments; cashback not counted.

A-L3: pay(ts, id, amount)->'payment<k>' (global counter)|None; 2% cashback (floored) credited at ts+86_400_000 before other ops at that ts; get_payment_status(ts, id, payment)->'IN_PROGRESS'|'CASHBACK_RECEIVED'|None (None also when the payment belongs to another account).

A-L4: merge_accounts(ts, id1, id2)->bool (balance, outgoing totals, pending cashbacks and payment ids move to id1; id2 removed); get_balance(ts, id, time_at)->balance after all ops at time_at, None if the account did not exist then; merged account inherits history.

B-L3: transfer(from, to, amount) puts funds on hold; transfer_accept(transfer_id) completes it (sender's available balance drops while pending, recipient unchanged). B-L4: merge_account(from, into) keeps histories and pending transfers; a merged-away id can be re-created later.
